bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro orders cut 15-20% on weak demand — multiple broker confirmation
bullets.body: Nikkei Asia reports Apple instructed suppliers to cut iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders by 15-20% for October, unusually early in the cycle. Higher retail prices ($100 increase) and surging memory chip costs are cited as demand headwinds. SWKS (~60% Apple exposure), Qorvo (~50%), and SITM (~1% quarterly revenue headwind) are flagged as most at-risk; QCOM insulated given only ~10% Pro/ProMax modem share.

bullets.title: LITE: Optical components sold out through early 2029; AI server demand overwhelms supply
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO confirmed optical components for AI servers are completely sold out through early 2029, with the company unable to meet approximately 70% of demand through next year. This is a direct bullish read-through for AAOI and COHR. Hedgeye and multiple desks note this as a long catalyst for AAOI and SITM into the OCP conference.

bullets.title: ANET: Citi initiates Buy at $248 PT; Etherlink SU-144 opens $10B scale-up networking TAM
bullets.body: Arista launched Etherlink SU-144, a pure open-Ethernet scale-up networking solution competing against NVDA's NVLink and UALink. Citi values ANET at $248 (36x 2028 EPS, 17.6% upside) and cites MSFT collaboration on Maia accelerators and META on scale-out as key customer anchors. Dell'Oro estimates the ESUN TAM at $10B by 2027.

bullets.title: NET: Oppenheimer raises PT to $430 from $380; 3Q expected well above guidance
bullets.body: Oppenheimer lifts Cloudflare's PT to $430 on 15-20% YoY contract value growth, with Workers appearing in 50-75% of 3Q contracts. Management is expected to raise CY26 revenue guidance to 34-35% at the 3Q print. KeyBanc VAR survey confirms open-weight model shift continues to benefit NET as a cost-effective alternative.

bullets.title: T, VZ: SpaceX $8B 800 MHz spectrum acquisition triggers 5-7% pre-market selloff
bullets.body: SpaceX agreed to acquire Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum portfolio for ~$8B, addressing Starlink Mobile's indoor penetration gap and signaling intent to become a fourth US mobile carrier. AT&T -6-7%, Verizon -5-7%, TMUS -7.4% in pre-market. Morgan Stanley models <1% US mobile penetration by 2030 scaling to ~7% by 2035 (primarily rural), while tower stocks (AMT, CCI, SBAC) rallied 6-8% on colocations upside.

bullets.title: NVDA: Supply chain checks strong; Taiwan exports +26% m/m to $29.9B in September
bullets.body: UBS and Wolfe checks confirm robust NVDA supply chain with September Taiwan export data surging 26% m/m to $29.9B. Vera Rubin systems are on track; lower HBM density for Rubin Ultra reflects supply constraints rather than performance trade-offs. NVDA is rationing HBM amid strong accelerator unit supply. Hedgeye maintains bullish signal with range $225-$243.

bullets.title: DELL: Clear OEM leader in server execution; 3Q datacenter revenue +50% YoY with $500M unbilled backlog
bullets.body: JPM channel check with a large US VAR shows Dell is the best-positioned OEM in server supply chain execution, with 3Q26 datacenter revenue up ~50% YoY and ~$500M in unbilled backlog expected to ship in 2027. 4Q26 softness is characterized as mechanical pull-forward, not structural, with solid 1Q-3Q27 visibility. SMCI flagged with GPU-export scrutiny risks.

bullets.title: NOW: Elite partner channel check shows 10-25% AI SKU spend uplift on all renewals
bullets.body: A JPM discussion with an elite ServiceNow partner confirms all renewing customers are migrating to new AI SKUs with 10-25% average spend uplift (mostly to Advanced tier). Q3 landed on plan, Q4 tracking 35-40% of annual bookings, and the partner expects 2027 growth to exceed 2026 driven by new SKUs plus consumption revenue ramp.

bullets.title: NFLX: Planning ~5% workforce reduction (~850 employees), announcement as early as next week
bullets.body: Netflix is preparing a restructuring to be announced as early as next week, impacting approximately 5% of its workforce (~850 workers). Hedgeye's risk range on NFLX is bearish at $66-72. The layoffs appear cost-driven rather than demand-related.

bullets.title: GOOGL: JPM sees $50-100B EBIT upside in 2028 from Anthropic TPU sales — mid-$20s EPS bull case
bullets.body: JPM argues TPU sales to Anthropic could reach 10GW by 2028, generating $50-100B EBIT vs. Street's $270B total 2028 EBIT estimate. Bulls model mid-$20s 2028 EPS vs. consensus ~$18. GOOGL also launched Gemini Agent for Work (orchestrating across Gemini and Claude) and is positioned as a funding short for HFs long META/AMZN, adding tactical appeal.

bullets.title: MSFT: Bullish signal maintained; Surface Laptop Ultra launches at $2,599 with 128GB unified memory
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains MSFT in bullish signal range $506-535. Surface Laptop Ultra launched at up to 128GB unified memory at $2,599. Trump admin's H-1B visa suspension for major tech firms (including ACN, CTSH) is flagged as a support for domestic tech headcount, though Microsoft itself is named in the suspension list.

bullets.title: META: Bullish signal $709-755; bans ByteDance ads in 7 countries; strong 3Q print expected
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains META bullish with risk range $709-755. Jefferies notes META is well positioned for a strong Q3 print with CY26 capex expectations >$250B. META also banned ByteDance advertisements across its apps in 7 countries, escalating TikTok rivalry, and is collaborating with ANET on scale-out networking solutions.

bullets.title: AMZN: Hedgeye shifts to bearish; Leo satellite program weeks from launch with 3x downlink advantage
bullets.body: Hedgeye changed AMZN's trend signal from Neutral to Bearish (range $240-259). On the fundamental side, JPM notes AMZN's Leo satellite program is weeks away from launch with 396 satellites in orbit and 3-8x performance advantages vs. Starlink on downlink/uplink — a potential competitive response in broadband.

bullets.title: DIS: Wolfe raises PT to $132; cost cuts fund DTC growth, 23% upside flagged
bullets.body: Wolfe raises Disney PT to $132 (prior $131) on FY28 EPS of $8.49, citing ~$300M annualized savings from ~1.5K YTD layoffs being reinvested into DTC. Disney's TV/streaming business has ~50K employees vs. Netflix's ~16K, pointing to further efficiency runway. DIS trades at 14x FY27 EPS, ~10% discount to the S&P.

bullets.title: LYV: Top live entertainment pick; Venue Nation fan growth exceeding 10M, AOI above consensus
bullets.body: Wolfe maintains LYV as top pick in live entertainment, with concerts AOI estimates ~$20M above Street for the quarter and Venue Nation fan growth expected to exceed 10M (vs. 5M annually in prior four years). Live entertainment YTD +21.3% vs. S&P +13.4%; sector trades at 21% discount to its 3-year average EV/EBITDA of 15.2x.

bullets.title: HPE: PC market collapse (-20% YoY in 3Q26) creates significant headwind; Morgan Stanley flags 41% revenue decline risk
bullets.body: Global PC shipments fell 20.1% YoY to 62.7M units in 3Q26 — the second consecutive annual decline and worst quarter since COVID — driven by 1H26 inventory pull-forward and memory cost-driven price hikes. Morgan Stanley forecasts HPE revenue down 41% in 2027. Apple was the only OEM to gain share (+90bps to 9.5%).

bullets.title: AI ARR debate: OpenAI $50B Sept run-rate, targeting $70B by year-end — capex cliff risk if industry misses $400-600B by end-2027
bullets.body: FT's report of $50B OpenAI ARR (vs. prior $70B expectation) caused a mid-day AI selloff before Bloomberg clarified it as a run-rate-vs-target methodology difference. OpenAI still guides to $70B annualized by year-end and is raising $30B+ at a $1.4T valuation. The broader concern: the AI buildout requires $400-600B in industry ARR exiting 2027 to justify 2029/2030 capex plans (~$1.4T), and missing that marker creates a 'capex cliff' risk weighing on multiples.

bullets.title: TSLA, NVDA, AAPL: Hedgeye maintains bullish risk ranges into 4Q; GOOGL, AMZN bearish
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Oct 9 Risk Range signals: NVDA bullish $225-243, MSFT bullish $506-535, TSLA bullish $345-390, META bullish $709-755, AAPL bullish $332-344; GOOGL bearish $337-352, AMZN bearish $240-259, NFLX bearish $66-72. Net long exposure among consensus US L/S HFs hit the lowest level of 2026.

bullets.title: WULF, HUT: Morgan Stanley NDR for TeraWulf (WULF) Oct 14 in NYC; no rating change
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley scheduled a TeraWulf NDR with CEO for October 14 in New York. No new rating action, but the event provides a near-term catalyst window for positioning.

bullets.title: CRWV: JPM hosted joint equity/credit CoreWeave call; Piper bullish on job posting demand trends
bullets.body: JPMorgan held a joint equity and credit discussion on CoreWeave addressing capital structure questions. Piper's morning call separately flagged CRWV job postings as reflecting positive demand trends in infrastructure software, alongside CSCO.
